blocks.text: Superposition of two waves having the same frequency and travelling in the same direction results in phenomenon called interference.

blocks.alt: Speakers S1 and S2, joined through P.A. to A.G., send out circular wavefronts: magenta arcs from S1, cyan arcs from S2; solid arcs are compressions and dashed arcs rarefactions. Points P1, P3 and P5 lie where like arcs cross; P2 and P4 lie where a solid arc crosses a dashed arc.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.5 (b): Interference of sound waves (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.5 (b)).

blocks.text: An experimental set up to observe interference effect of sound waves is shown in Fig. 7.5(a). Two loud speakers S₁ and S₂ act as two sources of harmonic sound waves of a fixed frequency produced by an Audio Generator (AG). Since the two speakers are driven from the same generator, therefore, they vibrate in phase. Such sources of waves are called coherent sources. A microphone attached to a sensitive Cathode Ray Oscilloscope (CRO) acts as a detector of sound waves. The CRO is a device to display the input signal into waveform on its screen. The microphone is placed at various points, turn by turn, in front of the loud speakers as shown in Fig. 7.5(b).

At points P₁, P₃ and P₅, we find that a compression meets a compression and a rarefaction meets a rarefaction. So, the displacement of two waves are added up at these points according to the principle of superposition and a large resultant displacement is seen on the CRO screen (Fig. 7.5-c).

blocks.alt: A CRO screen with a scaled cross showing a large wave of big displacement.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.5(c): Constructive Interference: Large displacement is displayed on the CRO screen (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.5(c)).

blocks.alt: A CRO screen with a scaled cross showing only a flat line along the horizontal axis.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.5(d): Destructive Interference: Zero displacement is displayed on the CRO screen (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.5(d)).

blocks.title: Example 7.1
blocks.problem: Two speakers are arranged as shown in the figure. The distance between them is 3.0 m and they emit a constant tone of 344 Hz. A microphone P is moved along a line parallel to and 4.0 m from the line connecting the two speakers. It is found that tone of maximum loudness is heard and displayed on the CRO when microphone is on the centre of the line and directly opposite to each speaker. Calculate the speed of sound.
steps:
Distance between speakers S₁S₂ = 3.0 m
Tone frequency f = 344 Hz
Distance between speakers and line of motion of P   S₁P = 4.0 m
Speed of sound v = ?
For tone of maximum loudness or the condition for constructive interference, the path difference must be 0, ±1λ, ±2λ, ±3λ, …
At middle point 'O' the path difference between two sound waves is zero (S₁O = S₂O), thus at that point 'O' constructive interference takes place.
For the next point P of constructive interference, the path difference between waves should be λ. So,   λ = path difference = S₂P₁ − S₁P₁

Now, we calculate values of S₂P₁ from right angle triangle S₁S₂P₁
S₂P₁ = √((S₁S₂)² + (S₁P₁)²)   (By Pythagoras Theorem)
S₂P₁ = √((3)² + (4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 m

Therefore,   λ = S₂P₁ − S₁P₁   or   λ = 5 − 4 = 1 m
This is the path difference for constructive interference.
blocks.answer: Putting the values, we have   v = 344 × 1 = 344 m s⁻¹

blocks.title: Example 7.2
blocks.problem: The wavelength of a signal from a radio transmitter is 1500 m and the frequency is 200 kHz. What is the wavelength for a transmitter operating at 1000 kHz and with what speed the radio waves travel?
steps:
λ₁ = 1500 m = 1.5 × 10³ m,   f₁ = 200 KHz = 2.0 × 10⁵ Hz
f₂ = 1000 KHz = 1 × 10⁶ Hz,   λ₂ = ?,   v = ?,   As v = fλ

Since, the speed of both the signals is same, so
v = f₁λ₁
v = 2.0 × 10⁵ × 1500
v = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹

Also   v = f₂λ₂
λ₂ = v/f₂
λ₂ = (3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)/(1 × 10⁶ Hz)

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text:
Monochromatic Light
Sodium chloride in a flame gives out pure yellow light. This light is not a mixture of red and green.
